query: Identify this anonymized tourist attraction from detailed geographic, historical, and visual clues: Baidicheng, or the unnamed site fortified site, is an old fortified site and religious site complex positioned on a hill by the Yangtze waterway in China. Baidicheng or the unnamed site fortified site is an old fortified site and religious site complex on a hill on the northern shore of the Yangtze waterway in China, 8 km east of the present day Fengjie County seat in Chongqing municipality. The religious site complex is now on an island, due to raised water levels following the construction of the Three Gorges Dam. Many older structures were submerged, and new buildings have been built higher up. The religious site complex island is linked to the north bank of the Yangtze, by a bridge. The island continues to be a tourist attraction, with many cruise ships halting for tours at Fengjie.[citation needed] The unnamed site is also known by another local name, because so many poets such as Li Bai wrote about it (see: "Departing from the unnamed site in the Morning"). Baidicheng is an old fortified site and religious site complex situated on an island in the Yangtze waterway, recognized for its historical importance and poetic heritage.

Find the tourist attraction from visual, scene, geographic, and historical clues: The Qianwang religious site is a historical site in Hangzhou, China, dedicated to the Qian dynasty. It contains beautiful grounds and is situated near the scenic West Lake. The religious site of the Qian Kings, also known by its Chinese name as the Qianwang or Qian Wang religious site, is a Chinese religious site in Hangzhou, China, honoring the Qian family who ruled as kings of Wuyue in the 10th-century interregnum between the Tang and Song dynasties. Owing to the general lack of plural markers in Chinese, it is frequently understood as a religious site specifically honoring Qian Liu, the first of the Wuyue kings, but it officially honors his entire dynasty. The grounds include the tomb of Qian Liu as well as four of his children and are located beside the Park of Orioles Singing in the Willows. The restored religious site has been reckoned among the Ten New Scenes of West Lake under the name ”Loyalty Displayed at the Qian religious site“. A Taoist religious site was first constructed at the site to honor the Qian kings of Wuyue in Yuanfeng 2 (1079) during the Song dynasty.
